AccessibilityConfig.description: Alt text, subtitles and contrast settings for accessible outputs.
AccessibilityConfig.title: AccessibilityConfig

ApiConfig.description: The local HTTP API bind address, authentication and request limits.
ApiConfig.title: ApiConfig

BrandKitConfig.description: Colours, fonts, logo, watermark, intro/outro and caption style.
BrandKitConfig.title: BrandKitConfig

BudgetConfig.description: Spending caps, provider monthly limits, alert thresholds and policy.
BudgetConfig.title: BudgetConfig

CharacterConfig.description: Consistency chain, QA thresholds, consent flags and reference limit.
CharacterConfig.title: CharacterConfig

CharacterConsentConfig.description: Rights flags that gate voice cloning and real-person likeness.
CharacterConsentConfig.title: CharacterConsentConfig

CharacterQAConfig.description: Thresholds and retries used to accept a character-consistent asset.
CharacterQAConfig.title: CharacterQAConfig

CircuitBreakerConfig.description: Failure threshold and cooldown for one provider circuit.
CircuitBreakerConfig.title: CircuitBreakerConfig

ConsistencyStrategy.description: How a scene may be made consistent with a character.
ConsistencyStrategy.title: ConsistencyStrategy

ContentProfileConfig.description: Everything a run needs to produce content for one audience or brand.
ContentProfileConfig.title: ContentProfileConfig

DatabaseConfig.description:
The SQLite file inside the user data directory and its busy timeout.

``filename`` is a bare file name; the directory is always the user data
directory so a config file cannot point the database at another location.
``busy_timeout_ms`` is how long SQLite waits for a lock before raising
``database is locked``.
DatabaseConfig.title: DatabaseConfig

DeliveryConfig.description:
Delivery providers, the fallback chain and shared retry settings.

Providers may be nested under ``providers`` or written directly as
``folder``, ``link``, ``email`` and ``webhook`` keys. The ``chain`` lists
provider names in fallback order and every entry must name a provider.
DeliveryConfig.title: DeliveryConfig

DeliveryProviderConfig.description:
Fields shared by every delivery provider.

Provider-specific fields are present but only the ones relevant to the
selected ``type`` are used. Credentials are referenced by name.
DeliveryProviderConfig.title: DeliveryProviderConfig

DownloadPolicy.description: Whether remote references may be downloaded.
DownloadPolicy.title: DownloadPolicy

DurationRangeConfig.description: Inclusive lower and upper bounds for a generated video in seconds.
DurationRangeConfig.title: DurationRangeConfig

DurationRangeOverrideConfig.description: A partial duration range used by platform and profile overrides.
DurationRangeOverrideConfig.title: DurationRangeOverrideConfig

ExamplesConfig.description: Liked and disliked examples that steer topic and writing choices.
ExamplesConfig.title: ExamplesConfig

FormatRecipeConfig.description:
An ordered recipe that selects stages, options and output handling.

``stages`` keeps its declared order. ``capabilities`` lists the operations
the recipe needs, ``output_type`` describes the final artifact and
``handler`` says whether it is saved, published or delivered.
FormatRecipeConfig.title: FormatRecipeConfig

FormatsConfig.description:
Named format recipes.

Recipes may be written directly under the section
(``formats: {narrated_still: {...}}``) or nested under ``formats`` (or
``recipes``); every form validates to the same mapping.
FormatsConfig.title: FormatsConfig

JobsConfig.description: Worker concurrency, retry and heartbeat settings for the job queue.
JobsConfig.title: JobsConfig

LLMConfig.description: Provider chain, per-role models, token prices and the repair limit.
LLMConfig.title: LLMConfig

LanguageConfig.description: Settings for one language written natively from the shared fact base.
LanguageConfig.title: LanguageConfig

LanguagesConfig.description:
The available languages plus the one used when none is requested.

A config file may write the language entries directly under the section
(``languages: {en: {...}, de: {...}}``) or nest them under ``languages``;
both forms validate to the same model.
LanguagesConfig.title: LanguagesConfig

NameVerifyConfig.description:
How often a generated name is transcribed and checked before accepting.

Verification regenerates the spoken name up to ``retries`` times when the
transcription does not match within ``threshold``.
NameVerifyConfig.title: NameVerifyConfig

OccasionConfig.description:
One config-defined personalization type, such as a birthday.

``variables`` are the fields an order of this occasion may fill.
``personalization_levels`` restricts which order levels are allowed, while
``files`` lists optional prompt or template files shipped with a custom
occasion.
OccasionConfig.title: OccasionConfig

OccasionVariableConfig.description:
One variable a personalized occasion asks the customer to provide.

A bare name is accepted as shorthand. ``type`` selects the validation the
order input applies, ``required`` marks mandatory fields and ``default`` is
used when an optional variable is omitted. Choice variables list their
allowed ``options``.
OccasionVariableConfig.title: OccasionVariableConfig

OccasionsConfig.description:
The configured occasions and the one selected by default.

Occasions may be written directly under the section
(``occasions: {birthday: {...}}``) or nested under ``occasions``.
OccasionsConfig.title: OccasionsConfig

OnExceed.description: What to do when a budget cap is reached.
OnExceed.title: OnExceed

OnRateLimit.description: What a token bucket does when the next token is not available yet.
OnRateLimit.title: OnRateLimit

OrderPricingConfig.description:
Currency, line-item amount and one flat tax estimate for receipts.

This is deliberately not a tax engine: ``tax_rate`` is a single flat rate
and receipts state that they are not tax invoices (decision D-011).
OrderPricingConfig.title: OrderPricingConfig

OrdersConfig.description: Personalized order defaults: levels, name verification and pricing.
OrdersConfig.title: OrdersConfig

OutputHandler.description: What happens to the final artifact once a run succeeds.
OutputHandler.title: OutputHandler

OutputType.description: The kind of final artifact a format recipe produces.
OutputType.title: OutputType

PersonalizationLevelConfig.description:
One personalization level: the stages it runs and what it costs.

``stages`` is the ordered subset of pipeline stages the level runs.
``price`` is the line-item amount before the flat tax estimate. The feature
flags say which optional order variables the level uses.
PersonalizationLevelConfig.title: PersonalizationLevelConfig

PipelineConfig.description: The ordered stages a pipeline runs and the timezone used for schedules.
PipelineConfig.title: PipelineConfig

PlannerApprovalMode.description: Whether a plan needs human approval before it executes.
PlannerApprovalMode.title: PlannerApprovalMode

PlannerConfig.description: Step, iteration, approval, tool, preview, default and budget settings.
PlannerConfig.title: PlannerConfig

PlannerDefaultsConfig.description:
Values applied in batch mode when the instruction omits them.

The common plan settings are typed for discoverability. Additional
settings are accepted and kept as attributes so a format or tool can add a
default without a core release.
PlannerDefaultsConfig.title: PlannerDefaultsConfig

PlatformAccountConfig.description: One publishing account, bound to exactly one platform and language.
PlatformAccountConfig.title: PlatformAccountConfig

PlatformsConfig.description:
Publishing accounts keyed by ``platform/language``.

Entries may be written directly under the section
(``platforms: {youtube/en: {...}}``) or nested under ``accounts``.
PlatformsConfig.title: PlatformsConfig

PresetConfig.description:
A named set of configuration overrides selected by the CLI or a profile.

A preset may name the content profile it belongs to. When the configured
profiles are available, a non-empty profile is checked against them so a
typo never silently selects the default profile.
PresetConfig.title: PresetConfig

PresetsConfig.description:
Named presets keyed by name, with an optional default preset.

Entries may be written directly under the section
(``presets: {short: {...}}``) or nested under ``presets``.
PresetsConfig.title: PresetsConfig

PrivacyConfig.description: Redaction and personal-data handling for logs, prompts and sidecars.
PrivacyConfig.title: PrivacyConfig

ProfilesConfig.description:
Named content profiles.

Profiles may be written directly under the section
(``profiles: {short: {...}}``) or nested under ``profiles``; both forms
validate to the same mapping.
ProfilesConfig.title: ProfilesConfig

ProviderConfig.description:
One named provider instance used by router chains.

``type`` names a registered provider type or a dotted import path.
``options`` are passed to the adapter unchanged. ``secret_refs`` maps an
option name to the secret reference that supplies its value; the reference
is resolved through the secrets loader, never stored here.
ProviderConfig.title: ProviderConfig

ProvidersConfig.description:
Named provider instances keyed by the names router chains use.

Entries may be written directly under the section (``providers: {fal: {...}}``)
or nested under ``providers``. Every entry must name a non-empty ``type``.
ProvidersConfig.title: ProvidersConfig

PublishAccountConfig.description: One publishing account and the secret references it needs.
PublishAccountConfig.title: PublishAccountConfig

PublishConfig.description: Publishing accounts, dry-run policy and reference validation.
PublishConfig.title: PublishConfig

QualityConfig.description: Thresholds and retry policy for generated media quality assurance.
QualityConfig.title: QualityConfig

RateLimiterConfig.description:
Default rate and on-limit policy for a provider token bucket.

``requests_per_minute`` is the sustained rate used when a provider does not
declare its own limit. ``burst`` is the largest short-term allowance and
``0`` falls back to the sustained rate. ``on_limit`` chooses between
waiting for the next token and raising a rate limited error.
RateLimiterConfig.title: RateLimiterConfig

ReferenceConfig.description: Similarity level, similarity gates, regeneration cap and downloads.
ReferenceConfig.title: ReferenceConfig

ReferenceDownloadConfig.description:
Limits and policy for fetching remote reference URLs.

``mode`` decides whether a remote reference is fetched, confirmed or
rejected. ``max_bytes`` caps the response body, ``timeout_seconds`` caps a
single request, and ``max_redirects`` bounds redirect chains when
``follow_redirects`` is enabled. A cached download is reused unless
``cache`` is disabled.
ReferenceDownloadConfig.title: ReferenceDownloadConfig

RenderConfig.description: Deterministic renderer settings that never require an AI call.
RenderConfig.title: RenderConfig

RetentionConfig.description:
How long intermediates, cache, logs and personal data are kept.

Final outputs are pinned and are never removed unless
``delete_final_outputs`` is explicitly enabled.
RetentionConfig.title: RetentionConfig

ReviewConfig.description:
Approval policy for the optional human review stage.

``approval_mode`` is ``always`` (a reviewer must approve every run),
``ask`` (the default: approve unless a profile says otherwise) or ``never``
(skip the review stage). When a review is not answered before
``timeout_seconds``, ``on_timeout`` decides whether it is rejected,
approved or only escalated with a notification.
ReviewConfig.title: ReviewConfig

SafetyConfig.description: Prompt and media screening before a paid or published call.
SafetyConfig.title: SafetyConfig

ScheduleConfig.description:
Named cron schedules, their timezone and the default entry.

Entries may be written directly under the section
(``schedule: {daily: {...}}``) or nested under ``schedules``. A single
top-level ``cron`` and ``profile`` pair is treated as the ``default`` entry.
ScheduleConfig.title: ScheduleConfig

ScheduleEntryConfig.description: One cron entry: when to run and which content profile to use.
ScheduleEntryConfig.title: ScheduleEntryConfig

ScoringConfig.description: Versioned rubric, dimension weights and score thresholds for research.
ScoringConfig.title: ScoringConfig

SimilarityLevel.description: How closely generated content should follow the reference.
SimilarityLevel.title: SimilarityLevel

StageConfig.description:
One ordered pipeline stage with its recipe-specific options.

A stage may be written as a bare string (``write``) or as a mapping with a
``stage``/``name``/``id`` field and an optional ``options`` mapping. The
shorthand ``{write: {mode: facts}}`` is accepted too.
StageConfig.title: StageConfig

StorageConfig.description:
Where generated media and intermediates are stored.

Credentials are referenced by name and resolved through the secrets
loader, never written into the configuration file.
StorageConfig.title: StorageConfig

TokenPricing.description: USD prices for one million input and output tokens of a model.
TokenPricing.title: TokenPricing

TracingConfig.description: Optional tracing export; disabled by default and vendor neutral.
TracingConfig.title: TracingConfig

VariableType.description: The value type a personalized order variable accepts.
VariableType.title: VariableType

VideoConfig.description: Video defaults shared by formats, profiles and platform overrides.
VideoConfig.title: VideoConfig

VideoOverridesConfig.description: Partial video settings applied on top of the base video section.
VideoOverridesConfig.title: VideoOverridesConfig

WordsPerSecondConfig.description: Inclusive speaking-rate bounds used to estimate and check script length.
WordsPerSecondConfig.title: WordsPerSecondConfig
